procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The order of the Tribunal was challenged before the High Court in Writ Petition Nos. 13617-13627/2017 & 14529/2017 and Writ Petition No. 11342/2017. The High Court set aside the order of the Tribunal.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The parties appealed the High Court's decision to the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court disposed of the appeals, allowing the High Court to direct re-evaluation of scripts or sustain the cancellation of the written examination results. The Supreme Court did not express any opinion on the merits of the rival contentions, leaving it open to the High Court to decide the matter, preferably within three months.

issue.issue_text: Whether the written examination can be sustained as being free from any irregularity, with only the interviews being held again.

facts: The case involved a selection process by the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) for Group ‘A’ and Group ‘D’ posts.
The entire selection process, including written exams and interviews, was annulled by the State Government due to widespread complaints of malpractices, bribes, and irregularities.
The High Court upheld this annulment, citing evidence of corruption such as call details between candidates and KPSC members, identical interview marks being awarded, and destruction of evidence.
Before the Supreme Court, some parties argued that the written examination itself was not tainted and should be saved, with only the interviews being conducted again.
law: A court can remand an issue back to a lower court for consideration, especially if the contention was not raised or decided in the original proceedings.
application: The Supreme Court noted that the specific argument to separate the written exam from the tainted interviews had not been raised before the High Court.
Rather than ruling on the merits of this new argument, the Supreme Court permitted the parties to file an application with the High Court to have this specific issue examined.
The Court explicitly stated that it was expressing "no opinion on merits" and was leaving the decision entirely to the High Court.

The Supreme Court instructed the High Court to examine the issue and gave it several options: it could restore the written exam results if they were found to be free from blemish, order a re-evaluation of the scripts, or uphold the cancellation of the written exam.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court did not decide the issue itself. Instead, it referred the matter back to the High Court for a decision on the merits, as the argument had not been raised there previously. The Supreme Court empowered the High Court to determine whether the written examination was free from irregularity and could be sustained.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the written examination can be sustained as being free from any irregularity, with only the interviews being held again.
appellant_arguments: The written examination is not vitiated by any irregularity and can be sustained.
Only the interviews need to be held again, not the entire selection process.
respondent_arguments: The written examination is not vitiated by any irregularity and the same can be sustained. Interviews can be held again.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: A decision to cancel a selection process can only be interfered with if it is found to be patently arbitrary, malafide, or illegal.
obiter: The appointment of ineligible, inefficient, or persons of questionable integrity has a serious adverse impact on the working of the Government and is anathema to the rule of law.
The best selection for Government service is a mandate of the Constitution.
No right accrues to candidates merely by being on a select list.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The Supreme Court did not decide the merits of whether the written examination could be sustained. Instead, finding that this specific contention was not raised before the High Court, the Court permitted the parties to raise the issue by moving the High Court. The Supreme Court directed the High Court to then examine the contention on its merits, explicitly stating, "We do not express any opinion on merits of the rival contentions which will be open to be gone into by the High Court."
legal_tests_applied: The Supreme Court did not apply a legal test to the merits of the case; its reasoning was procedural, based on the principle that arguments should be raised in the appropriate lower court before being considered on appeal.
why_appellant_lost: The appellant did not secure a final order from the Supreme Court reinstating the written examination because the Court determined this specific argument had not been raised before the High Court. Consequently, the Court remanded the issue for consideration by the High Court rather than deciding it directly.
why_respondent_won: The respondent succeeded in so far as the Supreme Court did not overturn the High Court's decision to annul the selection process. By remanding the matter for the High Court to consider the new argument, the cancellation of the selection remains in effect pending that review.
policy_considerations: The High Court's reasoning, noted in the judgment, highlights that the "appointment of ineligible, inefficient or persons of questionable integrity has serious adverse impact on the working of the Government and is anathema to the rule of law," and that ensuring the "Best selection to Government service was the mandate of the Constitution."
